comments.body:
## Evidence extended from 2 runs to 11 (2026-09-15)

This ticket was filed on the first two four-arm runs (`ts-carbon`, `scss-uswds`). The four-arm
set is now **eleven** runs, all judged on the same protocol by three independent classifiers with
majority aggregation. The defect reproduces throughout, and is **worse** than the original
+21% suggested.

I duplicated this ticket by mistake while working the larger set — `arbored-demurrable-whippet`
(`0110-bb37-caea-4d47`), now linked `duplicates` and closed. Its evidence is consolidated here.

### Totals

**164 emitted findings → 137 distinct issues, +19.7%.** Per run:

| run | emitted | distinct | inflation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rb-spree-tax-provider-interface` | 25 | 15 | **+67%** |
| `ts-carbon-dsx-card-web-component` | 15 | 10 | +50% |
| `ts-strata-paidleave-rfi-staff-experience` | 15 | 11 | +36% |
| `ruby-mn-deed-casemgmt-outbound-writeback` | 9 | 7 | +29% |
| `jira-dso-legacy-code-remediation` | 18 | 15 | +20% |
| `java-opensearch-adaptive-concurrency` | 19 | 18 | +6% |
| `jira-dso-strata-sdk-planning-context` | 19 | 18 | +6% |
| `scss-uswds-elements-dsx-token-migration` | 20 | 19 | +5% |
| `java-gradle`, `java-iceberg`, `ts-strata-sdk-cm-signal-coverage` | — | — | 0% |

`rb-spree` is the new worst case at **+67%** (11 `same_arm_merges`, 8 duplicate groups, three of
them three-member). Three runs show 0%, so the behaviour is not unconditional.

### 24 duplicate groups across 8 runs

Beyond the five already recorded here, the nine added runs contribute (finding id [criteria]):

- **`rb-spree`** (8 groups): `fe9362212ee777e1b`[E1,COH]+`fe4973736fd1cec19`[E3] · `f4bd59683171f9ef2`[E4]+`fee2ecdefb4a472fd`[G1G2] · `f808aa9b1ff1a1a44`[G1G2]+`f9787d46f01fa1024`[G6] · `fd2ab9187e0f1af59`[E1,E6]+`f867ddb18c92babcc`[T2]+`f733d5b9d1c96f596`[E5] · `fb6f563673ec04b82`[A1]+`f5bfe8629b7309691`[E4] · `fa97557f732cede1d`[T4]+`f9a1fafd8662260f0`[T11]+`f1cb101798e624148`[T11] · `fdac6206d2c64d0d5`[T5a]+`fb617713d8f0ac36b`[T5b] · `fbcd188a4af1f9c5c`[G6]+`f88e7e6caacfdf7a1`[E4]
- **`ts-strata-rfi`** (4): `f02d0cd5760121153`[T5b,T9]+`f50f3f76a15e65bc6`[G6] · `fd2b4ab546f9e330c`[T1]+`f252cc4922c662cc3`[T5c] · `ff1e44af24964e2c6`[E4]+`f711f89314e759479`[G1G2]+`ff433167f9a0c74c5`[G6] · `f71d6f4d69d9eda6e`[T5b]+`fa13c03bbc6396a28`[T6]
- **`jira-dso-legacy`** (2, both 3-way): `fefb33dc413d1ffce`[E2,T2]+`ff3ca4c59c47d2605`[T5a]+`f979dd7afcdc2675a`[G6] · `f183d47c0909708aa`[E2]+`fa60c9c99e3cf1eb4`[T5b]+`f979dd7afcdc2675a`[G6]
- **`java-opensearch`** (2): `f5b48e0266cef5b37`[E2,E1]+`f45ee8af458d5e534`[A1] · `fec86f00ba47d9527`[G1G2]+`f6df8eee7ef8c8679`[T3]
- **`ruby-mn-deed`** (2): `fbda6e01e068e5510`[COH]+`f4439faeb93f9d19d`[E1] · `f8c8cc7182e9ee590`[E4]+`f72dae17551bf761a`[G1G2]
- **`scss-uswds`** (2 further): `fa397c3a9c775bb37`[E2]+`f2fe1f5b397e2040f`[G1G2] · `f8fbdb6fdf4b8abc3`[COH,E6]+`f164935f57c7fe71a`[G6]
- **`jira-dso-strata`** (1): `f596c92c78cf6b105`[G6]+`faf7819abb3a020d4`[T8]

### Criteria pattern, and one case that breaks it

A specific criterion pairing with a **generic** one recurs: `G1G2` (edit-set/scope accuracy) or
`G6` (approach soundness) appears in **13 of the 16** groups outside spree. But `rb-spree` group
12.1 has **two members carrying the SAME criterion, `T11`** — so cross-criterion emission is not
the whole mechanism.

One finding can duplicate two different defects at once: `f979dd7afcdc2675a` [G6] is a single
`dso-legacy` finding merged into **two** separate issues.

### Fingerprints still do not match

Every genuine duplicate pair across all 11 runs has **distinct** finding ids. There is no
per-finding fingerprint to compare — `material_fingerprint` exists once per run at the verdict
top level, not per finding.

One apparent counterexample, stated so it is not misread: `rb-spree` ballot parts `2.1` and `2.2`
share id `f4bd59683171f9ef2`. That is **one** finding the ballot split into two parts, not two
findings colliding.

### Drop reasons: three now, none of them deduplication

The `rfi` verdict's 7 drops are all `veto:cited-reference-inaccurate`; the `spree` verdict's 7
are `low-validity` and `veto:absence-refuted`. Three distinct reasons across two sampled
verdicts, and **no finding in any run was dropped for duplication**. The drop mechanism fires
readily; it just never fires for this.

### Blocking

Confirmed across the wider set: **28 member findings carry `decision=block`** (22 in the first
ten runs, 6 in spree), with several groups blocking on *every* member — `scss-uswds` 1.1/3.1,
`ts-carbon` 2.1/3.1, `rfi` 3.1/6.1, `mn-deed` 2.1, `dso-strata` 1.1, `java-opensearch` 5.1,
`rb-spree` 2.1/4.1. Duplication inflates the blocking count an author must answer.

### Divergent blocking eligibility within one issue

More instances of copies of one issue disagreeing on whether they can block: `rfi` 12.1
(`blocking_enabled=false, threshold=0.95` vs `true, 0.6`), `java-opensearch` 3.2, `dso-legacy`
10.1 and 14.1, `ts-carbon` 9.1, `mn-deed` 1.1, and `rb-spree` 1.1, 11.1, 23.1.

### Reproduction

Verdicts `~/plan-review-bakeoff/wave3/rebar-runs/<run>.verdict.json`; judge-majority merges in
`~/plan-review-bakeoff/artifacts/adjudications/<run>.adjudication.json` (`merged_issues`,
`arms.rebar.same_arm_merges`). Regenerated by `harness/fourarm_report.py`.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## Measured: the duplication is real, and it is a design consequence rather than a defect

Background investigation complete. Read-only; no writes to code or the store.

### Scale

- **5,772** `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecars scanned.
- **502 of 4,349** reviews (**11.54%**) contain at least one candidate cross-criterion duplicate group — the same underlying issue reported once per criterion that touches it.
- Against a hand-adjudicated benchmark: **164 findings for 137 distinct issues — +19.7% row inflation.**

So roughly one review in nine shows the pattern, and where it appears it inflates the finding count by about a fifth. That is large enough to change how a plan author experiences the gate — a single structural problem arrives as three or four separate demands — and small enough that it is not corrupting the majority of reviews.

### Mechanism — four independent places, none of which is wrong on its own

1. Pass-1 **fans criteria into separate finder calls** (`orchestrator.py:248-251`, `pass1.py:434-442`).
2. Each call **can only attribute to its own criteria** (`passes.py:242-257`). A finder that sees an issue spanning three criteria has no vocabulary to say so.
3. Pass-3 **decides each row independently** (`decide_ops.py:292-303`), so it never sees the rows as siblings.
4. Dedup is **exact-match and criterion-scoped** (`review_kernel/decide.py:240-246`), so near-identical text under different criteria is by construction not a duplicate.

The fan-out is what gives each criterion focused attention, which is why review quality is good. The duplication is the cost of that same choice. There is no single line to fix — the finding has no home because the model has no concept of "one issue, several criteria".

### What is NOT in question

This is not a correctness bug. Every duplicated row is a true finding against the criterion that raised it. Nothing is being reported that is not there.

---

**Decision: whether the reviewer should model an issue as a first-class unit, or keep criterion-scoped rows and reduce the noise downstream.**

- Duplication rate is 11.54% of reviews, +19.7% rows where it occurs.
- All four contributing sites are individually correct; the gap is the absent "fix unit" concept.
- The fan-out that causes it is also what produces the per-criterion focus the gate depends on.
- Options 1 and 2 change what authors see; options 3 and 4 change only how much.

Which do you want?

**(1) Introduce a first-class fix-unit grouping — findings that share a root cause are emitted once with the criteria they satisfy listed, so an author fixes one thing and clears several criteria at once. Largest change; addresses the cause rather than the symptom.**

(2) Add a Pass-3 cross-criterion consolidation step that merges sibling rows after the fact — keeps Pass-1's fan-out untouched, but the merge is heuristic and will sometimes merge two genuinely distinct issues.

(3) Relax dedup from exact-match to similarity-scoped across criteria — smallest change, removes the most obvious repeats, leaves rephrased duplicates in place.

(4) Leave the behaviour and document it — the gate output states that one issue may appear under several criteria, so authors read a group of related rows as one fix. The +19.7% inflation stays.

comments.body:
## Measured: the existing fix-unit grouping (citric-alert-dogfish, 5e64) has never fired

Main already carries a cross-criterion grouping step for BLOCKING findings: `_group_blocking_fix_units` in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/floors.py`, keyed by `sidecar.fix_unit_key` = sha256(token-set(location) + "|" + token-set(finding text)), criteria-free, stamp-only (`group_id`, `is_primary`, `group_criteria`; every member keeps `decision=block`; only the CLI renderer collapses). The discovery-stage `review_kernel.suppress_and_dedup` (bug 5e40 B2) is criterion-scoped by its documented key and does not apply here.

The key requires the two findings' significant-token SETS to be identical for both location and text. Independent finder calls reword both, so it never matches:

- All 9,756 local `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecars: 5,838 persist the `group_id` field; **0** carry a stamp; **0** have two blocking findings sharing a `fix_unit_key` on recompute.
- carbon Group A (the 3 blocking members E4/G1G2/T1): 3 distinct keys; pairwise text token Jaccard 0.33-0.48, location 0.27-0.46. The T3 member is advisory, which 5e64 scoped out of grouping.
- Bakeoff join (31 adjudicated runs with a matching verdict; the join recovered 16 judged-duplicate pairs from 3 runs, fewer than the 24 groups in the comment above): `fix_unit_key` equal on **0/16**.

No lexical rule tried separates duplicates cleanly on blocking pairs (10 duplicate, 84 non-duplicate): text Jaccard >= 0.35 catches 2/10 with 0 false merges; shared cited path + text Jaccard >= 0.15 catches 5/10 with 6/84 false merges. Choosing a detection rule is a design decision; no code changed.

comments.body: Measured 2026-11-02: evidence proximity as a pre-filter for duplicate detection. Data: the 24 judge-confirmed duplicate groups (arbored-demurrable-whippet) across 8 bakeoff runs, verdicts under ~/plan-review-bakeoff (wave3/rebar-runs and superseded/pre-remediation-reviews/wave3/rebar-runs); 39 duplicate pairs vs 1,217 other same-run pairs. 'Proximate' = the two findings share a cited file path or basename (location + evidence) or a backticked symbol. Duplicates: 21/39 (54%) proximate. Others: 46/1217 (3.8%) proximate. So the filter cuts comparisons from 1,256 to 67 but misses 18/39 duplicate pairs; 13/39 duplicate pairs have a member citing no file at all (plan-prose locations, typically the generic G6/G1G2 member). Script: .rebar/scratch/a85e3cd3-prox/prox.py in the main checkout. Related prior art: bakeoff LINKAGE.md section 2 rejected pairwise same-issue votes plus connected components because findings asserting several problems chain unrelated issues (188 of 1,596 multi-finding issues); its adopted method groups one arm's findings in a single set-level call (step B). f979dd7afcdc2675a in jira-dso-legacy-code-remediation is such a bridging finding (member of 2 groups).

comments.body: Operator decision 2026-11-02: option (18). Add one grouping call over a review's BLOCKING findings, run only when there are 2 or more, modelled on the bakeoff's step-B set-level grouping (LINKAGE.md section 2-3: one call sees all findings and returns groups; no pairwise votes, no transitive chaining). Groups stamp the existing citric-alert-dogfish fields (group_id, is_primary, group_criteria); every member keeps decision=block and only the CLI collapses. A finding may belong to at most one group. Advisory findings stay out of scope. Supersedes the lexical fix_unit_key grouping, which never fired (0 of 9,756 sidecars).

## Offline eval of the grouping prompt (2026-11-02), Gerrit change 3242

Ran the production prompt `plan-review-fix-unit-grouping` through the real runner (Bedrock, the standard model class `_verifier_cfg` resolves, temperature 0) over the 8 bakeoff verdicts that hold the 24 judge-confirmed duplicate groups (same verdict selection as `.rebar/scratch/a85e3cd3-prox/prox.py`). Script: `.rebar/scratch/a85e3cd3-snowyowl/eval_grouping.py` in the worktree; results in `eval-results.json` beside it. The call saw the findings only, as in production (no plan text).

**Production mode — BLOCKING findings only (what ships):**
- Judged duplicate pairs with both members blocking: 15. Grouped: **13 of 15** (87%).
- Other blocking pairs in the same verdicts: 104. Falsely merged: **3** (2.9%).
- Invalid answers (fail-open path taken): 0 of 8 calls.
- Per run (blocking findings / judged pairs / hit / false merge): rfi 7/4/4/0, carbon 7/4/4/0, dso-legacy 4/0/0/0, uswds 8/2/2/0, opensearch 7/1/1/1, mn-deed 4/1/1/0, dso-strata 4/1/1/0, spree 5/2/0/2.
- Both misses and 2 of the 3 false merges are in rb-spree: the model regrouped 4 blocking findings across the two judged groups (fee2ecdefb4a472fd with f9787d46f01fa1024; fe9362212ee777e1b with f4bd59683171f9ef2) instead of the judged (f4bd59683171f9ef2, fee2ecdefb4a472fd) and (f808aa9b1ff1a1a44, f9787d46f01fa1024). The third false merge is java-opensearch f92b6304f04d09171 + faf9a816e511a41da (two AC-verifiability findings).

**Capability probe — blocking + advisory together (not shipped; advisory is out of scope):**
- 39 judged pairs, 27 grouped (69%); 17 false merges among 1,192 other pairs (1.4%).
- 1 of 8 answers was rejected by validation (jira-dso-legacy: the model put one finding in two groups, which the bridging finding f979dd7afcdc2675a invites); the fail-open path stamped nothing, as designed.

Group stamps are counted at pair level: a false merge pair means two findings would share a `group_id` and the CLI would fold one under the other; both still block and stay in the sidecar.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Plan review emits one defect as several BLOCKING findings, one per criterion that touches it
(evidence in this ticket's comments: 164 emitted findings for 137 distinct issues across 11
judged bakeoff runs, 24 judge-confirmed duplicate groups, 28 duplicate members carrying
`decision=block`). Plan authors therefore see the same blocking defect counted several times.

Main already has a stamp-only grouping seam for blocking findings,
`_group_blocking_fix_units` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/floors.py:197`, called at
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:526` after the floors and cross-checks, before
`_finalize_signature`), which stamps `group_id`, `is_primary`, `group_criteria`, and a CLI
renderer that collapses a group to its primary (`src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:486-503`).
Its key, `sidecar.fix_unit_key` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:321`), needs identical
token sets and has never matched: 0 of 9,756 local `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecars carry a stamp.

Operator decision 2026-11-02 (option 18, recorded in this ticket's comments): replace the
lexical key with ONE set-level grouping LLM call over the BLOCKING findings.

## Approach

One structured sub-call, modelled on the bakeoff's step-B within-arm grouping
(`~/plan-review-bakeoff/LINKAGE.md` sections 2-3): a single call sees all blocking findings
and returns the groups that state the same defect. No pairwise votes, no transitive
chaining, and a finding belongs to at most one group. A set-level call fits this problem
because the duplicates are rewordings across criteria that no lexical key catches (the
measured lexical rules caught at most 5 of 10 duplicate blocking pairs), and pairwise
linking with connected components chains unrelated issues through compound findings
(LINKAGE.md section 2).

The call follows the existing post-decide sub-call idiom in
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/xcheck.py` (`_assess_contradictions`, line 183): a library prompt
file with `category: plan-review-pass`, a pydantic structured-output contract registered via
`contracts.register_contract`, a `RunRequest.for_structured(...)` request on the standard
verifier class (`_verifier_cfg`), greedy sampling (`temperature=0.0`, as
`floors._score_floor_novelty` does) so a re-review re-groups the same way, and fail-safe
exception handling. It stays at the existing seam rather than becoming a
`gates/plan-review.yaml` workflow step because the Pass-3 floors and cross-checks that run
after the workflow can still drop blocking findings; grouping after them means no group can
name a dropped finding.

Behaviour of `_group_blocking_fix_units(verdict, *, ctx, cfg, runner, repo_root)`:

1. Fewer than 2 blocking findings, or blocking ids not unique: no call, no stamps.
2. One call with each blocking finding listed by `id`, criteria, location and text.
   Output contract `plan_review_fix_unit_groups`: `{"groups": [{"defect": str,
   "members": [finding ids]}]}`.
3. Validation, fail open: if the call raises, returns a non-list, names an id not in
   the blocking set, or puts one id in two groups, emit NO groups and log a warning.
   Groups with fewer than 2 distinct members are ignored.
4. Stamping keeps the citric-alert-dogfish contract unchanged: each member of a valid group
   gains `group_id` (`"g"` + first 16 hex digits of sha256 over its sorted member ids) and
   `is_primary`; the primary (existing rule: highest priority, then alphabetically-first
   sorted criterion, then lowest id; missing priority sorts as 0.0) gains `group_criteria`
   (sorted criteria union). Every member keeps `decision=block` and stays in
   `verdict["blocking"]`; the verdict string, counts and buckets do not change.
5. Accounting: `verdict["coverage"]["fix_unit_grouping"]` records `status`
   (`grouped` / `no_groups` / `failed`), `groups` (count) and the call's `_usage`.
   The runner's existing usage log and step-failure tally cover the call like any
   other sub-call. When no call is made, coverage is untouched.

Advisory findings stay out of scope.

`sidecar.fix_unit_key` itself is NOT deleted: the criterion-effectiveness harness uses it as
its cross-round match key (`evals/plan-review-gate/harnesses/criterion_effectiveness.py:271`).
Only its use as the grouping key is removed, with no lexical fallback.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/floors.py` — replace the lexical grouping with the sub-call,
  its contract model and registration, validation and stamping.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` — pass `ctx`, `cfg`, `runner`, `repo_root` at the
  call site.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` — add the `PASS_FIX_UNIT_GROUPING` prompt id beside
  `PASS_COMMENT_TRAIL` (line 153).
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_fix_unit_grouping.md` — new prompt file.
- `tests/unit/test_blocking_fix_unit_grouping.py` — rewrite the grouping tests on
  `FakeRunner`; keep the `fix_unit_key` unit tests.
- `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` — add the new `RunRequest` site to the
  census (`_EXPECTED_RUN_REQUEST_SITES`, count 20 to 21).
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — one paragraph on blocking fix-unit grouping.

## Testing

Unit tests with `rebar.llm.runner.FakeRunner(structured=...)` and a recording runner:

- happy path: a returned group stamps `group_id`/`is_primary`/`group_criteria`, all members
  remain in `blocking` with `decision=block`, verdict string unchanged;
- 0 or 1 blocking findings: the runner is never called;
- fail open: runner raises; output names an unknown id; one id in two groups; malformed
  `groups` — each leaves no stamps and an unchanged verdict;
- primary tie-breaks (existing rule), sidecar persistence via `build_payload`, CLI collapse.

Offline eval (not a CI test): run the production prompt through the real runner
(`AWS_PROFILE=frontier-bedrock`) over each bakeoff run's blocking findings for the 8 runs
holding the 24 judge-confirmed duplicate groups, and score recall on judged duplicate
blocking pairs and false merges on other blocking pairs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_blocking_fix_unit_grouping.py` passes, including tests that
      (a) stamp a group from FakeRunner output, (b) make no runner call with fewer than 2
      blocking findings, (c) emit no stamps for a raising runner, an unknown id, an id in
      two groups, and malformed output, and (d) assert the verdict string and the blocking
      list length are unchanged in every case.
- [x] `git grep -nF 'fix_unit_key' -- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/floors.py` returns no
      lines (the lexical grouping is gone), and `sidecar.fix_unit_key` still exists for the
      eval harness.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py tests/unit/test_plan_review.py
      tests/unit/test_plan_review_sidecar.py` passes.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0 (module-size, complexity and mechanism
      ratchets included).
- [x] The offline eval's recall and false-merge counts are recorded as a comment on this
      ticket (no financial figures).
- [x] The Gerrit change carries `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` and is merged.
